root_cause.text: mt7921_roc_abort_sync() synchronously cancels roc_work with cancel_work_sync() while the caller may already hold dev->mt76.mutex, but roc_work itself runs under that same mutex, creating a lock inversion deadlock in the mt76/mt7921 ROC work path.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly states “roc_work() holds dev->mt76.mutex, while cancel_work_sync() waits for roc_work() to finish” and that this happens during station removal via mt7921_mac_sta_remove() -> mt7921_roc_abort_sync(); the patch removes cancel_work_sync(), first claims ROC ownership with test_and_clear_bit(MT76_STATE_ROC, ...), and switches to non-blocking cancel_work() to avoid waiting while the mutex may be held.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix ROC abort handling by returning early when ROC is inactive, clearing ROC state up front, and always resuming interfaces without synchronously waiting on ROC work.
intent_record.what: The function now first calls test_and_clear_bit(MT76_STATE_ROC, &phy->mt76->state) and returns immediately if the bit was not set, removes the conditional wrapper around ieee80211_iterate_interfaces(), changes cancel_work_sync(&phy->roc_work) to cancel_work(&phy->roc_work), and unconditionally calls ieee80211_iterate_interfaces() after deleting the timer and canceling the work when ROC state had been set.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now exits early when no ROC operation is active, and when ROC is active it clears that state before proceeding, cancels pending ROC timer/work without waiting for the work handler to finish, and always resumes interfaces as part of ROC abort. This prevents duplicate state clearing logic and ensures the resume path runs exactly for active ROC cases.

grouping_result.intent: Fix ROC abort handling by returning early when ROC is inactive, clearing ROC state up front, and always resuming interfaces without synchronously waiting on ROC work.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly modify ROC abort behavior to avoid synchronously waiting on ROC work and to clear ROC state safely, which addresses the deadlock root cause caused by cancel_work_sync() interacting with roc_work under the same mutex.

candidates.rationale: This is the direct deadlock trigger: it synchronously waits for roc_work completion even when the caller may already hold dev->mt76.mutex, while roc_work itself needs that same mutex, creating the lock inversion described in the root cause.

The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is present directly in this function: `cancel_work_sync(&phy->roc_work);`. This function contains no guard, lock-state check, deferred cancellation, or any alternative non-blocking handling to avoid calling `cancel_work_sync()` in that context. The vulnerable construct is present: `mt7921_roc_work()` explicitly acquires the device mutex via `mt7921_mutex_acquire(phy->dev);` before doing ROC abort work, and `mt7921_abort_roc()` calls `cancel_work_sync(&phy->roc_work);`. The caller `mt7921_cancel_remain_on_channel()` acquires the same mutex first with `mt7921_mutex_acquire(phy->dev);` and then calls `mt7921_abort_roc(phy, mvif);`. This creates the deadlock pattern described in the root cause: a thread holding `dev->mt76.mutex` calls `cancel_work_sync()` on `roc_work`, while `roc_work` itself needs that same mutex to complete. Therefore the bug is present. There is no protective handling in this code to avoid calling `cancel_work_sync()` while the mutex is held, nor any restructuring to release the mutex before cancellation or make the cancellation asynchronous, so the fix is not present.
